chapter: Judgments on Ellington, Parker and others
title: Non-New Orleans musicians Rose admires
summary: Rose names Lips Page, Lucky Roberts, Pee Wee Russell, Bobby Hackett and Hodes as musicians he liked or respected though they weren't from New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Are there any musicians that do not relate so much to the New Orleans style that you are particularly impressed by or with?

Yeah, of course, I was much impressed with Lips Page, whom I consider to be a great individual artist. I was impressed with Lucky Roberts, who's, I suppose, not only because of his music, but because of the environment of that place and that time. I was, of course, impressed with Pee Wee Russell, whom I was very fond of personally. That's a guy that I always enjoyed having around. And, of course, these are not New Orleans folks. I like, there were a lot of musicians that I liked personally whose music I didn't like at all, which is even more common. But I consider that there were a lot of great musicians who weren't from New Orleans, like Hody's, for example.

Mm-hmm. And there are musicians like Bobby Hackett, for example, who's spectacular. but whose approach to music doesn't, I don't respond to emotionally at all. It's not my kind of thing. Although I respect him and his work. You see, I know...
For the same reason, you don't respond to Big Spider?
Yes, very much the same reasons then. So, I would say that there were quite a lot of musicians that I enjoyed. Of course, all of them... But the great ones
you weren't impressed by at all.
